data.hypothesis: Instantiating CUB BlockReduce with its commutative-only raking policy may reduce CTA-local reduction overhead for integer addition relative to the selected parent's default CUB policy. This is a contrasting local-policy test: the previous explicit warp-reductions CUB variant measured slower than the default parent. The 128-thread launch, one value per lane, zero-filled tails, multi-stage scratch schedule, and final copy remain fixed; only controller timings can establish whether this helps independently of launch topology.

memory_lessons.applicability: For this fixed reduction topology, the measured default CUB parent was faster than the measured explicit CUB warp-reductions variant; a distinct CUB policy is a reasonable next comparison, not an assumed improvement.
memory_lessons.claim: The selected parent measured 29.215 μs mean, while the explicit CUB warp-reductions candidate measured 29.729 μs mean; both were correct. The measurements do not establish why they differed.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the commutative-only CUB policy with the same launch and full-run protocol, including correctness checks.

data.notes: The candidate has not been measured. Prior supplied outcomes were correct for all 10 cases; the baseline mean was 46.7866 μs, the selected parent mean was 29.2154 μs, and other local-reduction candidates ranged near 29.49–29.73 μs. The controller must validate this policy and compare complete-run timings before concluding whether it helps. Scratch selection and final-copy behavior are unchanged.
transformations: Explicitly instantiate CUB BlockReduce with BLOCK_REDUCE_RAKING_COMMUTATIVE_ONLY for the block sum.
Retain one zero-filled value per lane for safe tails and leave the launch geometry, scratch-stage schedule, scratch selection, and final copy unchanged.
